# THE PRIMITIVE CENSUS — which public scalar primitives use only tested forms

*Generated by `scripts/primitive_census.py`. Do not edit.* Rebuild: `python3 scripts/primitive_census.py --src <dir> --fetch --out docs/PRIMITIVE-CENSUS.md` (needs `x86lean-diff` built, clang and network; the sources are cloned into `<dir>` at the commits below).

<!-- census-model: vectors=1198 forms=962 -->

## What this measures, and what it does not

A **form** is a printed mnemonic (width suffix, condition code and prefixes included) plus the class of each operand. The model side is the **1198** differential vectors, which execute **962** distinct forms. A candidate is **ALL COVERED** when every form its code executes is one of them and every addressing mode it uses is one some vector uses.

- **Addressing modes are checked separately, not ignored.** The model computes every effective address in one function (`Ea.offset`), so the mode is not part of the form; the modes the vectors exercise are `abs`, `base`, `base+index`, `fs:abs`, `fs:base`, `gs:abs`, `index`, `rip`, and a candidate mode outside that set is NOT COVERED. The `strict` column keeps the mode in the form, for a reader who does not accept the collapse.
- **Coverage is a precondition for a task, not a price.** Nothing here says a covered function can be proved at an acceptable cost.
- **The decoder is trusted to XED** (TRUSTBASE.md): an encoding difference that keeps the form is not a coverage difference here.
- **One compiler, one target, one set of flags:** `Apple clang version 21.0.0 (clang-2100.3.34.2)`, `-target x86_64-apple-macos13`, `-O2 -fno-stack-protector -fcf-protection=none -fno-asynchronous-unwind-tables -fno-jump-tables -DNDEBUG -w`, disassembled by `objdump` (LLVM). C candidates are built twice: the default (`-O2`, clang may vectorise into SSE) and `scalar` (`-O2 -fno-vectorize -fno-slp-vectorize`). A different compiler emits different forms.
- **Calls that leave the object** are listed and mark the row; a candidate that calls out is never counted as covered. Calls and tail jumps inside the object are followed and counted with the entry.
- **The reference column is not uniform.** Only the s2n-bignum and Vale rows measure the verified artifact itself; a HACL* row measures clang's compilation of verified C; the checksum rows have a specification and test vectors and no machine-checked reference was found.
- **A second instrument, in its own column (D332).** 69 forms of 27 mnemonics are in `siliconTable`: x86isa refuses them, so no differential vector can exist, and they are refereed by PROCESSORS instead (silicon: AMD EPYC 7763 + Intel Core i7-8700B (D334); AMD EPYC 9V45 + Intel Core i7-8700B (D335), hwprobe — NOT a semantic oracle; rows derived from the SDM's rules, the model pinned to the same rows by `decide`). That is NOT a semantic oracle — a processor agreeing on chosen rows is not a second model agreeing on the swept pre-states — so those forms are credited in a separately labelled column and verdict, **never in ALL COVERED**. The two counts may be cited side by side, never summed.

## The verdict: 42 of 57 candidates are ALL COVERED

By family: MAC **1** · bignum limb **26** · checksum **3** · field arithmetic **3** · hash (keyed) **2** · hash (non-crypto) **5** · hash compression **2**.

`instrs` counts the instructions the walk reached from the entry (calls and branches inside the object, and fall-through between an assembly file's labels); `unreached` is the rest of the object's code — for a one-routine `.S` file it must be 0, for a compiled file it is the file's other functions — printed so a short walk cannot pass as a small function. `strict` counts not-covered forms with the addressing mode kept in the form. **Same-register operands are not a dimension here** (`xorq %r8,%r8` is the form `xorq r64,r64`), and neither is which register is used.

## The silicon column, separately: 5 more candidates are COVERED WITH SILICON

**Referee: silicon: AMD EPYC 7763 + Intel Core i7-8700B (D334); AMD EPYC 9V45 + Intel Core i7-8700B (D335), hwprobe — NOT a semantic oracle.** A candidate is COVERED WITH SILICON when it is not ALL COVERED, does not call out of its object, uses only addressing modes the vectors use, and every form it lacks is a `siliconTable` form the processor probe executed. The verdict above is computed before these forms are loaded and the run refuses if any differential verdict moves after (D332).

**42 ALL COVERED (differential, x86isa) · 5 COVERED WITH SILICON (processors, hwprobe)** — two instruments, two counts, cited side by side and never added. COVERED WITH SILICON: `xxh3-64`, `vale-fmul`, `s2n-bignum_montmul_p256`, `s2n-bignum_mul_p25519`, `s2n-bignum_mul_4_8`.

## Appendix: every s2n-bignum x86 function

Of **332** functions in `s2n-bignum/x86/` (every `.S`, each its own entry), **206** are ALL COVERED. The not-covered ones, by the extension of the forms they miss (a function can count under more than one):

| missing class | functions |
|---|---:|
| BMI/ADX | 81 |
| base-ISA form untested | 39 |
| AVX/VEX | 20 |
| SSSE3/SSE4 | 1 |

**The silicon column, separately (silicon: AMD EPYC 7763 + Intel Core i7-8700B (D334); AMD EPYC 9V45 + Intel Core i7-8700B (D335), hwprobe — NOT a semantic oracle):** 67 of the 126 not-covered functions lack only silicon-refereed forms (COVERED WITH SILICON).
